title: The Clockmaker's Attic
revision_notes: Rev 1.3 (2026-07-18, POST-PLAYTEST TWEAKS -- Blind Playtester verdict READY-WITH-TWEAKS, all three tweaks USER-APPROVED at the step-6 checkpoint): TWEAK 1 (playtest 2a fork / designer flag #7 / Validator A1 RESOLVED): the p03/p04 pry clue-gates are KEPT (playtest confirmed ungating lets brute-pryers skip the cat and both watch chains), but the CORRECT board/brick now gives a FAINT-TELL on pre-clue prys -- a slight creak and perceptible shift, still firmly not yielding -- so an early pryer retains a memory hook instead of certifying the spot inert. Wrong spots keep the identical dead 'doesn't budge'. No-tell rule amended accordingly (no-tell for wrong spots everywhere; faint-tell ONLY for the correct pry spots pre-clue); new developer note D10. TWEAK 2 (playtest near-stuck): offering the mouse DIRECTLY to the cat no longer returns it with the generic refusal -- the cat locks eyes on the mouse, tail flicks, but stays put (mouse returns to inventory); every other item keeps the generic slow-blink return. Nudges toward wind-and-place-on-floor without executing it; D3/D4 updated. TWEAK 3 (playtest S2 bug-read): new partial-state feedback -- when WOUND and PENDULUM SWINGING but hands at any wrong time, the movement shows minimal life (soft escapement tick + occasional single hammer twitch that never strikes); full silence only when wind or pendulum is missing. Does NOT reveal the correct time; D9 easing valve stays dormant and untouched; solution stays front 7:20; strike grammar unchanged; new developer note D11. NOTHING ELSE MOVES: all solution values, dependencies, orderings, red herrings, and D9 are byte-stable from rev 1.2.

Rev 1.2 (2026-07-18, USER CHECKPOINT RULINGS): three changes. CHANGE 1 (flag #1 OVERRULED -- 'i'd prefer using IV'): all numerals level-wide are now STANDARD SUBTRACTIVE notation (IV, IX); the IIII convention and its teaching beat are removed everywhere (clu-face-convention node deleted; itm-tile-iiii renamed itm-tile-iv; p01 rewritten). p01's tray decoy is now a VI tile -- a modest non-RWK glyph-order wrinkle (IV vs VI), disproved in-scene by the dial's own seated VI; p01 gets slightly easier as permitted (designer z1 estimate 5.5 -> 5.0). CHANGE 2 (flag #6 modified): Dubai (Burj Khalifa, UTC+4) replaces Paris in the world-clock set per user ('add dubai for authenticity'); Tel Aviv, Tehran, Riyadh excluded per user. *** VAULT CODE CHANGED: p07 solution is now VI-X-I-III (was VI-VII-I-III). *** Same mechanism (master time 6:00 + stamped offsets), exactly one wrap case preserved (Tokyo 6+9=15->III). CHANGE 3 (flag #5 conditional keep): p09 mirrored-dial trap kept exactly as designed; a pre-planned overlay-only EASING VALVE is now SPECIFIED (developer_notes D9 + p09.easing_valve) but NOT implemented. All other checkpoint items RATIFIED as designed (#2 arithmetic peak, #3 p06 ungated, #4 12-hour wrap, #7 pry-sweep gating pending playtest). Everything the Validator verified at rev 1.1 is byte-stable except what these changes require. Producer: route p01/p07 deltas to the Validator for re-verification.

Rev 1.1 (2026-07-18): Validator Required Fix 1 applied -- example_ordering_C now explicitly lists the z4 free pickups ('take winding key + return tag') immediately after the z4 unlock and before p08/tag-inspect (the ordering as previously written could not complete; L1-Fix-1 class, example text only). NO solution value, dependency, zone, item, clue gate, or behavior changed.

Rev 1.0 initial design (2026-07-18). Adopts Level 1 rev-1.3 conventions as baseline: clue-gating with no-tell rule, uses-driven item lifecycle (declare every use; retain until all uses satisfied), non-collectible decoys (R6-003), requirement-flag state model (never step order), per-element overlay state rendering, container reveal/collect states, armed-item use, manual pickups.
theme: A tower clockmaker's attic workshop above the town. Every clock in the room stopped at the same moment. The attic backs directly onto the tower's great dial; the whole room is one connected machine of linkage rods, gears and chimes that the clockmaker left mid-thought. A gray cat still lives here.
framing_line: All his clocks stopped at six.
time_of_day: Late golden afternoon. Low warm sun through the dormer window (required: the cat's sunbeam patch, p02 staging); the great dial in z3 glows amber with transmitted daylight (required: mirrored-numeral legibility, p09).

win_condition.description: The attic's only exit, the stair door, is barred by a vault-style TIME LOCK connected by visible linkage rods to the tower movement behind the wall. Restore the great clock -- oil and wind it, set its hands to the release time shown on the clockmaker's 'will return' tag (set from BEHIND the mirrored dial), and start the pendulum. The strike train fires, the linkage lifts the door bar, and the player leaves down the stairs with the cat.

clue_gating.policy_revision: inherits L1 rev-1.3 policy (viewed_definition, persistence, D6/D7 semantics); no_tell_rule amended at rev 1.3 (playtest tweak 1, user-approved)
clue_gating.purpose: Protect code-like entries and sweep-brute-force surfaces from lucky/spoiler shortcuts while never false-blocking an earned solve. Gates reference only clues that carry the code's actual information.
clue_gating.viewed_definition: A clue counts as VIEWED the moment its designated close-up view has been displayed at least once. No dwell time, no comprehension check, no timers. Multi-instance clues count when ANY instance is displayed.
clue_gating.no_tell_rule: Gated attempts replay the puzzle's EXISTING failure grammar with no distinguishing tell -- IN FULL for p07 and p09, and for every WRONG spot at p03/p04. REV 1.3 AMENDMENT (playtest tweak 1): the CORRECT board (p03) and CORRECT brick (p04) are the single sanctioned exception -- a pre-clue pry there produces a FAINT-TELL (slight creak + perceptible shift, still firmly not yielding; see D10). Rationale: the playtest's impatient-pryer variant showed a pure no-tell on the correct spot lets an early pry CERTIFY the spot as inert, poisoning the later watch clue (15-25 min stall, 'the game lied to me'). The faint-tell leaves a memory hook without reading as an invitation. The code-entry gates (p07, p09) remain strictly no-tell.
clue_gating.ungated_rationale_class: Free pickups, tool-on-hotspot oiling, tile seating with pop-back, the cat beat, mechanism completions (winding, pendulum push), and the gear train (a mechanically TRUE configuration must work when built -- gating physical truth reads as a broken machine) are physical acts, not code entries.
clue_gating.art_impact: Rev 1.3: two micro-cues added, both SFX/haptic-tier plus one line of animation each -- the correct-spot faint-tell at p03/p04 (D10) and the cat's mouse-offer tell (D3). Everything else reuses existing failure states (wrong boards/bricks stay dead; vault wheels spin without the hatch releasing; hand-setting does not trigger the strike -- though see D11 for the wound+swinging ambient layer, which is state feedback, not gate feedback).

derived_conditions.name: timelock-release
derived_conditions.evaluation: Continuously evaluated boolean over three persistent states, TRUE the moment all three hold REGARDLESS of achievement order. On first TRUE it fires the strike beat and LATCHES state door-bar-raised permanently (later hand-fiddling cannot re-lock the door). This is a condition, never an event sequence. Rev 1.3: the D11 alive-wrong-time ambient (clock-wound AND pendulum-running AND NOT hands-at-release) is PRESENTATION derived from the same inputs -- it introduces no new state and never affects this condition's evaluation or latch.

nodes.content: Master clock stopped at exactly 6:00; case bears the same ★ as the Big Ben plate and the vault's Big Ben wheel header. Establishes reference time = 6.

Four hand-less clocks with landmark plates and stamped offsets: Burj Khalifa +IV, Big Ben ★ (reference), Fuji +IX, Liberty −V. With reference 6: Burj Khalifa 6+4=10, Big Ben 6, Fuji 6+9=15 -> III on a 12-hour dial (the single wrap case, ratified), Liberty 6−5=1. Landmark identification is NOT required -- pictogram matching to the vault headers suffices. (Rev 1.2: Dubai replaces Paris per user ruling; real offsets vs London: Dubai +4, Tokyo +9, New York −5.)

The great dial's numerals read mirror-reversed from behind -- the standing evidence that the back view is a MIRROR of the front, so the return tag's front-view 7:20 must be set as its mirror image. (Art: a mirrored IV reads as a malformed VI and vice versa -- see D1. The playtest confirmed the strongest passive tell is the ABSENCE of any legible 'VII' glyph on the back view.)
nodes.viewed_when: great dial close-up displayed (self-satisfying: the setting crank lives in this close-up)

nodes.content: Mini FRONT-VIEW dial fixed at 7:20 over a door pictogram: the time-lock's release time.

Visible linkage rods run from the stair door's time-lock bar along the ceiling into the wall, and re-emerge in z3 at the strike train: the door is opened BY the clock. Foreshadowing/orientation, not a gate.

Nudging the cat or offering ANY inventory item EXCEPT THE MOUSE gets the same terminal refusal: one slow blink, the cat resettles heavier on the cushion; offered items return unspent. Categorical ('this will never work'), identical on repeat, no escalation. REV 1.3 EXCEPTION (playtest tweak 2, user-approved): offering the TOY MOUSE directly produces a TELL -- the cat's eyes lock onto the mouse and track it, tail flicks, but it stays put; the mouse returns to inventory. Right idea, wrong verb: the tell nudges toward winding the mouse and setting it on the FLOOR without executing it (D3). Petting is allowed (purr, no state change). The only thing that moves a cat is prey -- moving prey.

nodes.name: The numeral-dial door
nodes.mechanic: environmental scavenger (4 hidden tiles) + positional numeral seating + glyph-order discrimination (IV vs VI decoy)
nodes.input: Seat numeral tiles into the four empty sockets (positions 2, 4, 7, 11).
nodes.derivation: Standard clock-face layout gives each numeral its position (the 8 seated tiles anchor it; the whole level uses standard subtractive notation -- rev 1.2 user ruling). The modest trap: the tray under the door offers a loose VI tile, inviting glyph-order confusion with the needed IV (I-before-V subtracts, I-after-V adds). The in-scene disproof sits on the dial itself: VI is already seated at position 6. Seating the tray VI in socket-4 whirs, stalls, and pops it back to the tray; seating IV completes the dial and trips the latch.
clues: 8 seated tiles anchor positions (incl. the seated VI at position 6 -- the tray decoy's standing disproof)

clue_gate.rationale: Physical seating with pop-back rejection, self-anchored by the 8 seated tiles. The only fork (IV vs the decoy VI) costs at most one extra attempt and is disproved by the dial itself -- gating would add friction for zero anti-spoiler gain. (Playtest: solved in ~6 min with one tray-tile mis-seat, self-corrected in seconds -- working as intended.)

nodes.failure_behavior: Wrong tile or wrong socket: whir-stall, tile pops back (inventory tiles to inventory, tray tile to tray). Unlimited attempts, correct seats persist.
nodes.notes: Rev 1.2: the IIII-convention trap is removed per user ruling; p01 is deliberately slightly easier now (compensating VI decoy kept modest per Producer instruction -- scope unchanged).

nodes.name: The cat and the mouse

nodes.solution_fixed: itm-toy-mouse wound and placed on the floor at the cat
nodes.derivation: The cat refuses everything else with the generic slow blink; the mouse specifically earns the locked-eyes/tail-flick tell (rev 1.3 -- right idea, wrong verb), and the cushion visibly has something flat beneath it. Wound and set on the floor, the mouse skitters; the cat pounces and chases it to the stair-door corner, keeping it -- and settles there for the rest of the level (by the exit).
clues: flat shape under cushion visible in close-up

clue_gate.rationale: Physical/character beat with a single affordance; the refusal grammar kills wrong theories categorically (L1 D4 lesson), and the rev-1.3 mouse-tell un-poisons the one refusal that used to punish the right idea (playtest near-stuck, ~5 min).

nodes.notes: Mouse is consumed by design (cat keeps it); it has no other uses. Placed anywhere but at the cat, it circles and returns to inventory; offered directly to the cat, it returns via the tell (D3/D4).

clue_gate.gate_behavior: REV 1.3 (playtest tweak 1): until watch A has been inspected, no board yields -- but the responses now differ by spot. WRONG boards: dead 'doesn't budge', identical every time (unchanged). The CORRECT board: a slight creak and a perceptible shift under the screwdriver -- still firmly not yielding, no visual change, no loose wobble (D10). Purpose: an early pryer keeps a memory hook ('that one FELT different') instead of certifying the correct spot inert; the faint-tell alone must not read as an invitation to keep grinding. After watch A is viewed: the correct board yields normally. Stale case: none (prying is an explicit act, re-attempted after viewing).
clue_gate.rationale: Gate KEPT per playtest 2a: ungating lets a brute-pryer obtain the great wheel before the slate and the oil can without ever moving the cat -- skipping the cat, both watches, and both carving-dial beats (the level's best chains). The faint-tell resolves the gated lane's poison (an early 'doesn't budge' on the correct board no longer contradicts the later clue). Watch A still carries the cache's entire location information; the gate cannot false-block an earned solve. (Flag #7 / Validator A1: RESOLVED, user-approved.)

nodes.failure_behavior: Wrong board (gated or not): dead 'doesn't budge', identical. Correct board while gated: faint-tell per D10 (creak + slight shift, refuses). No damage, unlimited attempts.

nodes.name: The automaton gear train
nodes.mechanic: gear-ratio reasoning (two-stage reduction; meshing train) -- LEVEL SIGNATURE MECHANIC (user ratified as the arithmetic peak, flag #2)
nodes.input: Mount one gear on POST A (meshing the crank's fixed 12-tooth pinion; POST A carries a fixed coaxial 8-tooth pinion) and one on POST B (meshed by that pinion, driving the cam). Then crank through one full cam revolution.

solution_fixed.arrangement: EITHER order -- 36 on A with 64 on B, or 64 on A with 36 on B (ratio product commutes; both are correct by design, multiple valid solves)

nodes.derivation: Slate: (A/12) x (B/8) = 24 -> A x B = 2304. Available: rack {16, 24, 36, 40, 48, 72} + the found 64-tooth great wheel. Unique pair anywhere in the level: 36 x 64 (the 36 is on the rack; the 64 must be found via p03 -- the great wheel is strictly required; the playtest confirmed 'no rack pair works, so a 64 must be hidden somewhere' lands as the intended deduction). The 48 tempts 48 x 48 = 2304 exactly, but only one 48 exists (rh-48-gear).
clues: stamped tooth counts (Arabic) + physically countable teeth on every loose gear
Roman XII / VIII stamps on the fixed pinions

live mechanical feedback: with ANY meshing pair mounted the crank turns and the cam/mural visibly runs at the resulting speed; the cam clack's cranks-per-clack cadence is countable (playtest 2b: the counting path is a legitimate no-algebra solve route)

clue_gate.rationale: Mechanical truth: a correctly built 24:1 train MUST work whether or not the slate was seen -- gating it would read as a broken machine. The brute-force surface (~30 ordered pairs, each needing a cranking test) is real but tedious, and the visible too-fast/too-slow cam feedback is INTENDED reasoning material, not a leak. User CONFIRMED ungated at checkpoint (flag #3).

yields.via: at exactly 24:1 the mural completes one full clean cycle (sun crosses the carved town, the watchman figure strikes his bell), a counterweight drops, and the wall panel swings open -- latches open permanently

nodes.failure_behavior: Wrong ratio: the cam visibly runs too fast or too slow; at cycle-end the panel latch ratchets and SLIPS with a clack (identical clack for every wrong ratio -- speed itself is the only differential feedback, by design). Gears freely remountable; rack gears return to the rack, the great wheel returns to inventory if unmounted. No lockout.

nodes.name: The four-wheel vault hatch (NUMERIC-CODE LOCK -- standing user directive honored)
nodes.mechanic: numeric combination lock; time-zone offset reasoning with cross-zone clue binding
nodes.input: Set four wheels (each engraved I-XII) under pictogram headers: Big Ben ★, Burj Khalifa, Liberty, Fuji.
nodes.derivation: REV 1.2 -- CODE CHANGED from VI-VII-I-III (Dubai replaces Paris per user ruling). Master clock (z1) stopped at 6:00 and shares the ★ with the Big Ben plate/header -> reference 6. z2 plates give offsets: Burj Khalifa +4 -> 10 (X); Liberty −5 -> 1 (I); Fuji +9 -> 15 -> III on a 12-hour wheel (the single wrap case, ratified at checkpoint, flag #4). Header order at the vault differs from the z2 row order, forcing pictogram matching. Landmark-name knowledge is never required -- pictograms match pictograms; the offsets are stamped in-world. Real-world offsets are authentic (Dubai UTC+4, Tokyo UTC+9, New York UTC−5 vs London).

clue_gate.gate_behavior: Wheels spin freely at all times; while gated the hatch stays shut on ANY setting including the correct one -- presentation-identical to a wrong code. Wheels retain position. Stale-correct-wheels case resolves via D6 re-evaluation on close-up entry. (Strict no-tell here is unchanged by the rev-1.3 pry-gate amendment.)
clue_gate.rationale: 12^4 = 20,736 combinations invites persistent fiddling and walkthrough spoilers; both gating clues carry the code's entire information and live in permanently reachable earlier zones (z1, z2), so no earned solve can be blocked.

nodes.failure_behavior: Wrong code OR gated attempt: hatch stays shut, identical. Wheels keep position; no lockout. (Playtest minor note, ships as-is per step-6 ruling: the hatch releases on being tried, not on the last wheel click -- a momentary bug-read the playtester rated cheap to survive.)

nodes.name: Oil and wind the movement
nodes.mechanic: mechanism completion (two-item: oil the dry drum bearing, then crank the winding key)
nodes.input: Oil can on the squealing drum bearing; winding key in the square socket; crank until the drive weight rises fully.
nodes.solution_fixed: itm-oilcan on drum bearing, then itm-winding-key in socket
clues: dry squeal + rust at the drum bearing; square socket visibly matches the key's square bit; drive weight visible on its line

clue_gate.rationale: Mechanism completion; both needs are self-evident (squeal, matching socket). Physical acts, not code entries.

yields.state_semantics: Persistent latched flag; drive weight fully raised. Feeds cond-timelock-release and the D11 alive-wrong-time ambient.

nodes.failure_behavior: Key before oil: key seats but won't turn, drum squeals -- oil need is restated diegetically. Nothing consumed. (The mouse's butterfly key visibly does not fit the square socket; offered anyway, it returns -- playtest confirmed this reads cleanly.)

nodes.name: Set the hands from behind (mirrored dial)
nodes.mechanic: clock-hands dial entry with a mirror-reversal inference -- clock hands as BOTH time and geometry
nodes.input: Turn the setting crank to position the great dial's hands (5-minute detents on the minute hand).
nodes.solution_fixed: mechanism (FRONT) time = 7:20; equivalently, the BACK view the player sees must show the mirror image of 7:20 (see developer_notes D1 for the rendering/state contract)
nodes.derivation: The return tag shows the release time 7:20 as a FRONT view. The player stands BEHIND the dial: numerals are visibly mirror-reversed (clu-mirrored-numerals), so naively copying the tag's hand positions onto the back view sets the front to 4:40 and nothing happens. The aha: mirror the tag (the playtest's unstick path: no legible 'VII' exists anywhere on the back view). Any-order verification: the strike fires the moment all three release conditions hold.

clue_gate.gate_behavior: Crank always turns and hands always move (a frozen crank would read broken); while gated, hands-at-release simply never asserts, so the condition cannot fire -- indistinguishable from having the wrong time set. clu-mirrored-numerals is self-satisfying (same close-up as the crank) and is deliberately NOT in the gate. Stale case: correct front-time set while gated, tag viewed later -- D6 re-evaluation on close-up entry (or on any subsequent state change) asserts the flag. (Strict no-tell here is unchanged by the rev-1.3 pry-gate amendment; the D11 ambient is state feedback about the MOVEMENT, not about the entered time's correctness.)
clue_gate.rationale: 144 detent combinations plus the tag being on the required path (z4 precedes any possible knowledge of 7:20) means the gate can never false-block; it closes the persistent-fiddling/spoiler path only.

yields.state_semantics: Continuously evaluated: TRUE while front-time = 7:20. Once cond-timelock-release latches, later hand movement is irrelevant (door bar stays raised).

nodes.failure_behavior: Any non-7:20 front time (including the un-mirrored 4:40 trap) OR gated state: the clock sits at that time and the strike does not fire. REV 1.3 (playtest tweak 3): if clock-wound AND pendulum-running, the movement now shows the D11 sign of life -- soft escapement tick + an occasional single hammer twitch that never strikes -- so the state reads 'alive, wrong input', never 'broken'. The ambient is identical at EVERY wrong time (it encodes nothing about closeness or the correct value). If wind or pendulum is missing: full silence, unchanged. Unlimited adjustment.
nodes.easing_valve: USER RULING (flag #5, 2026-07-18): trap KEPT as designed; the overlay-only softening specified in developer_notes D9 remains DORMANT and is untouched by rev 1.3 (the D11 ambient is a separate, weaker signal: it says 'wrong time', while D9 would help derive the RIGHT one). Activating D9 later must not change this node's solution, gate, or failure grammar.
nodes.notes: User checkpoint ruling: 'i feel it may be a bit hard but i'll have to play it to see, keep for now, with room to make it easier in future.' Playtest S2 (~10 min stall, hasty-reader worst case 15-30 min) is addressed at the bug-read level by D11; the inference difficulty itself is deliberately preserved.

nodes.name: Open the stair door and leave
nodes.mechanic: endgame free action once the time lock releases
nodes.input: When cond-timelock-release latches: the strike train fires (chimes), the linkage rods articulate along the ceiling in BOTH z3 and z1, and the door bar lifts. Return to z1, open the door.
clues: the cat, relocated to the door since p02, stands and stretches when the bar lifts (silent nudge)

clue_gate.rationale: Endgame free action; nothing to gate.

solve_path_notes.structure: Spine: z1 tile scavenge -> p01 -> z2. Then THREE parallel workstreams that cross-bind zones: (1) pointer-watch stream: watch A (z1 coat) -> dormer cache -> great wheel; mouse (z2) -> cat (z1) -> watch B -> chimney cache (z2) -> oil can; (2) machine stream: oil arbor -> gear train -> z3; (3) knowledge stream: view master time (z1) + world-clock row (z2) -> vault code. In z3: vault -> z4 (key + tag) -> endgame trio (wind / set hands / pendulum) in ANY order -> strike -> z1 exit. Any interleaving satisfying the requirement edges is valid.
example_ordering_A: take coat items (watch A + tile IV)
example_ordering_B_pendulum_first: view clu-slate-ratio AFTER experimenting at the frame (slate is confirmatory, not gating)
p08 (winding completes the trio -- condition latches here)
example_ordering_C_knowledge_first: view clu-master-time and note 6:00 before anything else
view clu-worldclock-row and pre-compute VI-X-I-III long before the vault exists
inspect watches A and B in either order
p04 then p03 (cache order is free)
p07 first thing in z3 (gates already satisfied) -> z4
take winding key + return tag (z4 free pickups)
solve_path_notes.state_model: All progression is satisfied-requirement flags (zone unlocked, item held, state latched, clue viewed) plus one derived condition (cond-timelock-release, an order-free AND over three states -- orderings B and C exercise different completion orders). No step-order tracking anywhere. p06 accepts BOTH gear arrangements (unordered set). Rev 1.3 adds NO new state: the D10 faint-tell and D11 ambient are pure presentation over existing flags.
solve_path_notes.revision_note: Rev 1.1 (Validator Required Fix 1): ordering C's z4 pickups made explicit; orderings A/B verified valid as written. Rev 1.2: ordering A's coat step now reads 'tile IV'; ordering C's pre-computed code updated to VI-X-I-III. Rev 1.3: no ordering changes -- the three playtest tweaks are presentation/feedback only.

developer_notes.note: Canonical clock state is FRONT time; solution_fixed is front 7:20. The z3 close-up RENDERS the back view: numerals and hand angles mirrored across the vertical axis (a front hour-angle of θ renders at −θ). The setting crank changes front time; the render stays consistently mirrored. Do NOT implement a second 'back time' variable. Art: mirrored numerals must be obviously reversed at close-up resolution -- this is the puzzle's entire evidence base. Rev 1.2 detail: with standard notation, a mirrored IV reads as a malformed VI (and vice versa), and VII / IX read distinctly backwards -- render the glyph mirroring crisply; it is the strongest reversal evidence on the plate (the playtest's actual unstick was noticing NO legible 'VII' exists on the back view -- preserve that absence exactly).

Re-evaluate on every change to clock-wound, hands-at-release, or pendulum-running, plus on z3 close-up entry (D6 stale case for p09). On first TRUE: play strike beat (chimes + rod articulation in the current zone), latch door-bar-raised permanently. Never gate on achievement order. Rev 1.3: the D11 alive-wrong-time ambient derives from the SAME three inputs (wound AND swinging AND NOT hands-at-release) -- implement it as a render/audio layer over the existing flags, never as new state, and stop it the moment the strike fires or an input drops.

developer_notes.topic: Cat refusal grammar + mouse-offer tell (rev 1.3, playtest tweak 2, user-approved)
developer_notes.note: Baseline (unchanged for everything except the mouse): nudging the cat OR offering ANY non-mouse inventory item produces the identical terminal refusal (one slow blink, resettles heavier); offered items return unspent; no escalation or variation across repeats. REV 1.3 EXCEPTION -- itm-toy-mouse offered DIRECTLY to the cat: the cat's eyes LOCK onto the mouse and visibly track it, tail flicks once or twice, body stays put; the mouse returns to inventory. Identical tell on every repeat (no escalation into pouncing -- the offer never executes p02). The tell is one line of animation distinct from the slow blink; its message is 'interested in THIS, but not like that', steering toward wind-and-place-on-floor. Petting: purr, no state change, always available. After p02 the cat sits by the stair door; baseline refusal grammar applies there (the mouse is gone by then, so the exception is moot).

Three mouse interactions, all loss-free until the solve: (1) offered DIRECTLY to the cat (armed-item use on the cat hotspot): D3 tell fires, mouse returns to inventory, p02 does NOT execute; (2) wound and placed on the floor anywhere NOT near the cat: skitters a small circle and returns to inventory automatically; (3) wound and placed on the FLOOR near the cat's bench: p02 fires, mouse leaves inventory permanently (cat keeps it -- it has no other uses; declared soft-lock-safe).

With any meshing pair mounted and the arbor freed, cranking runs the mural at the true resulting ratio -- visible speed IS intended feedback (mechanical truth, not a leak). Every wrong ratio ends its cam cycle with the SAME latch-slip clack; only speed differs. The cranks-per-clack cadence must be consistent and countable (playtest 2b: counting toward the slate's 24 tallies is a sanctioned no-algebra solve route). Gears mount/unmount freely; rack gears live in the apparatus (never inventory); the great wheel returns to inventory when unmounted. The fixed pinions (XII, VIII) are not removable.

Inherit L1 D6 verbatim: gated puzzles re-evaluate (gate AND solution) on every input/attempt event AND on entry into the puzzle's close-up. Stale cases here: p07 (wheels pre-set correctly while gated) and p09 (front 7:20 pre-set while gated). p03/p04 have none (pry is an explicit act).

Inherit L1 D7: one persistent saved boolean per gating clue (clu-watch-a, clu-watch-b, clu-master-time, clu-worldclock-row, clu-return-tag). Set on first display of the qualifying view; never cleared; ordinary satisfiable requirements. (Rev 1.2: the non-gating clu-face-convention flag is deleted with its node.)

The z1 stair door must never accept item use or code input: its housing has no keyhole (art requirement). Any interaction while barred: the bar rattles once against the linkage -- identical every time, pointing attention up the rods (the door teaches 'solve me elsewhere').

developer_notes.topic: p09 EASING VALVE -- SPEC ONLY, DO NOT IMPLEMENT (user ruling 2026-07-18, flag #5: 'keep for now, with room to make it easier in future'); STATUS AT REV 1.3: DORMANT, deliberately untouched by playtest tweak 3 (D11 is a separate, weaker signal -- it flags 'wrong time', D9 would help derive the RIGHT one)
developer_notes.note: Pre-planned softening for the mirrored-dial trap, designed now so a future 'make it easier' is a small staged change, not a redesign. THE VALVE: add a small wordless chalk sketch beside the setting crank on the EXISTING z3 close-up plate -- two mini-dials joined by a horizontal double-headed arrow, the left dial plain, the right dial its exact mirror image (the clockmaker's own working reminder that the back mirrors the front). STAGING: ships as a per-element overlay / crop-scoped edit on the existing plate (the standing L1 state-variant technique; no full-frame re-roll, est. cost one crop edit or $0 PIL), registered as a new optional clue node clu-mirror-chalk (non-gating, supports p09, viewed_when: setting-crank close-up -- self-satisfying like clu-mirrored-numerals). INVARIANTS WHEN ACTIVATED: solution stays front 7:20; p09's gate, no-tell rule, and failure grammar are untouched; no other node changes. Optional second tier if the first proves insufficient (design intent recorded, NOT specced for staging yet): make the return tag double-sided -- its reverse shows the mirrored dial; this would require new inventory-inspect art, so it is the fallback, not the valve. ACTIVATION AUTHORITY: user, at any post-release feedback round, via Producer to Developer + Asset Generation.

developer_notes.topic: Pry-gate memory hook (rev 1.3, playtest tweak 1, user-approved -- resolves flag #7 / Validator A1)
developer_notes.note: Applies ONLY to the two correct pry spots (p03 dormer board D3, p04 chimney brick at 9-o'clock) while their clue-gate is unsatisfied. Pre-clue pry on the CORRECT spot: a slight creak (SFX) + a perceptible shift (haptic-tier cue + ONE line of subtle animation -- a hair of movement under the blade), then the spot settles back, firmly not yielding. It must NOT read as an invitation on its own: no loose wobble, no gap opening, NO persistent visual change to the board/brick in any state or view -- the spot looks identical before and after. Pre-clue pry on any WRONG spot: the existing dead 'doesn't budge', identical every time (unchanged; this is the anti-sweep wall). Post-clue pry on the correct spot: yields normally (existing open animation). Purpose (playtest 2a): the early pryer's memory keeps a hook -- 'that one FELT different' -- so the later watch clue confirms rather than contradicts their experience; the wrong-spot wall still makes exhaustive sweeping unrewarding. The faint-tell is identical on every repeat (no escalation toward yielding).

developer_notes.topic: Alive-wrong-time movement feedback (rev 1.3, playtest tweak 3, user-approved)
developer_notes.note: New PRESENTATION state on the z3 movement, derived (never stored) from existing flags: ACTIVE when clock-wound AND pendulum-running AND NOT hands-at-release. Rendering: soft escapement tick (quiet, rhythmic, clearly mechanical) + an occasional single chime-hammer twitch that lifts slightly and settles WITHOUT striking (no chime sound ever). INACTIVE (full silence, hammers still): whenever wind OR pendulum is missing -- unchanged from rev 1.2. Terminates the moment the strike fires (cond-timelock-release latch takes over; strike grammar unchanged) or an input state drops. CONSTRAINTS: the ambient is IDENTICAL at every wrong time -- tick rate, twitch frequency, and animation never vary with how close the set time is to 7:20 and encode NOTHING about the correct value; it is not a gate tell (it renders regardless of clu-return-tag's viewed state, because it describes the MOVEMENT, not the entered code); D9 stays dormant and separate. Purpose (playtest S2 / hasty-reader 2c): the fully-restored-but-wrong-time state must read 'alive, wrong input', never 'broken' -- every subsystem giving positive feedback while the trigger stays silent was the bug-read that made the mirror trap feel unfair.

red_herrings.design: Rev 1.2 (replaces rh-iv-tile after the IIII convention was removed by user ruling): the tray under the door dial offers a loose VI tile -- glyph-order bait for the empty 4-socket (IV = one-before-five, VI = one-after-five). Honest and self-disproving: the dial's own seated VI at position 6 is permanently visible one glance away. NON-COLLECTIBLE: lives in the tray, seats-and-pops-back (whir-stall) from any socket. Fairness valve: worst case one extra attempt. (Playtest: cost seconds, taught the socket feedback -- rated 'fine'.)

48 x 48 = 2304 exactly -- the arithmetic works, inviting a hunt for 'the second 48'. Only one exists, anywhere. NON-COLLECTIBLE (rack gears never enter inventory); mounting the lone 48 with anything else gives honest wrong-speed feedback. Time-cost trap only; the 36 x 64 solution uses parts the player demonstrably has.

red_herrings.node: z2 display case of spare clock hands
red_herrings.design: The hand-less world clocks scream 'find and refit the hands'. The spare-hands case is screwed shut and painted over (inspect-only, NON-COLLECTIBLE contents); the world clocks accept no interaction. The stamped offsets on the plates are the actual payload -- the row is informational, not restorable. Defusal: categorical inertness from first contact, L1 feed-cup lesson. (Playtest: the false goal held ~40 min of game time and the screwdriver-in-hand makes the screwed case a magnet -- rated 'friction', ships as-is per the step-6 ruling; the secondary suggestion to make the paint-over one notch more emphatic in close-up is left to the Art Director's discretion.)

A clock-like brass dial that is not a clock: fixed needle, engraved sun/cloud/rain pictograms in close-up. Invites hand-setting/code theories; accepts no input. Pure time-cost; the pictograms make its non-clock nature legible without words. (Playtest: inspect-once, no time sink -- rated 'fine'.)

anti_softlock_invariants: No consumable can be wasted: the toy mouse is the ONLY by-design consumed item and has exactly one use (p02); anywhere else -- including offered directly to the cat (D3 tell) -- it returns to inventory (D4).

itm-screwdriver (2 uses), itm-oilcan (2 uses, never emptied), itm-winding-key, itm-great-wheel, all tiles until seated correctly: retained under the uses-driven lifecycle; nothing multi-use is consumed early (L1 poker lesson).

clock-wound and pendulum-running are persistent latches; hands-at-release is continuously evaluated; cond-timelock-release latches door-bar-raised permanently on first TRUE -- later hand movement cannot re-lock the exit.

All locks/codes (p01, p03, p04, p06, p07, p09) have unlimited attempts, no lockouts; wheels and hands retain position; gears freely remountable. The D10 faint-tell and D11 ambient are repeat-identical presentation cues that never consume, escalate, or lock anything.
Zones never re-lock (z2 door latch, z3 panel, z4 hatch all latch open permanently).

Every clue_gate references only clues in permanently reachable zones or inventory items on the required path (watches A/B, return tag are inspectable anywhere, forever); clue-viewed flags persist in the save (D7). So whenever a gated puzzle is reachable, its gate is satisfiable.
The cat cannot be harmed or blocked into an unwinnable state; it grants watch B exactly once; failed offers return items unspent (D3).

designer_difficulty_estimate.escalation_rationale: vs L1's 6.0: (1) two genuine multi-step inference chains with light arithmetic -- gear-ratio product (A/12 x B/8 = 24) and time-zone offsets with a 12-hour wrap; (2) longer dependency chains (mouse -> cat -> watch B -> chimney cache -> oil -> arbor -> gear train -> zone 3); (3) heavier cross-zone clue binding (z1 master time + z2 plates -> z3 vault; z1 slate -> z2 frame; watches found in one zone, applied in another); (4) one perceptual inversion (mirrored dial) with a designed trap answer (4:40). Difficulty comes from chain depth and layered reasoning, never pixel-hunting: every cache is anchored by an engraved ring, every code's data is stamped in-scene. Playtest verdict: 'the escalation is real' -- one derivation, one cross-zone synthesis, one perceptual reframe.
